guitar.label: Audio: RKO Radio interview, 8 Dec 1980. Picture: archive footage
subs: For five years I've been so locked in the home environment and completely switched my way of thinking that I didn't really think about music at all.
My guitar was sort of hung up behind the bed, literally.

sean.label: Audio: RKO Radio interview, 8 Dec 1980. Picture: archive footage
subs: And he just sat up and said, You know what I want to be when I grow up?
And I said, no, what's that? He looked me right in the eye and said, just a daddy.

bermuda.label: Audio: RKO Radio interview, 8 Dec 1980. Picture: archive footage
subs: And I called her because I was in Bermuda with Sean, and she was here in New York.
I said, well, look, we were talking about recording.
It must have triggered something off here, because I'm getting all this stuff.
And I started singing it to her down the phone or playing a cassette.

peebles_lennon.label: John Lennon, BBC Radio 1 interview, 6 Dec 1980 (heard in a UK TV tribute)
subs: And it took me two years to unwind. I can go out this door now and go in a restaurant.
Do you want to know how great that is? Or go to the movies.
I mean, people come up and ask for an autograph or say hi, but they won't bug you.

peebles_cam.label: Andy Peebles, BBC Radio 1 (UK TV tribute, Dec 1980)
subs: He just seemed a very, very happy and very involved person, and deeply in love with his wife.

r2.label: Audio: RKO Radio interview, 8 Dec 1980. Picture: archive footage
subs: Because it's still up to us to make what we can of it.
It's not out of our control. I still believe in love.
Peace. I still believe in positive thinking.

r4.label: Audio: RKO Radio interview, 8 Dec 1980. Picture: archive footage
subs: We all survived Vietnam, or Watergate, or the tremendous upheaval of the whole world that's changed.
We were the hip ones in the sixties, but the world is not like the sixties.
The whole map's changed, and we're going into an unknown future.
But we're still all here. We're still alive. There's hope.

martin.label: George Martin, the Beatles' producer (UK TV tribute, Dec 1980)
subs: Well, by the standards of great musicians, he wasn't a great musician, but he was a great man.
I mean, he was one of the originals of this century.

kfmb_speech.label: Balboa Park, San Diego, vigil, Dec 1980 (KFMB)
subs: It's not what he said twenty years ago, because he was where you were twenty years ago.
It's what he said in 1980. And what he was saying, and wanting to say, was hope.
And he was wanting to say, love your family.

r3.label: Audio: RKO Radio interview, 8 Dec 1980. Picture: archive footage
subs: And I consider that my work won't be finished until I'm dead and buried, and I hope that's a long, long time.
